skill.name: apktool
skill.description: Guides authorized Android APK reverse engineering with apktool. It covers decoding APKs, reviewing manifests, searching resources and smali, and rebuilding signed test APKs.
skill.summary: Decode, inspect, and rebuild Android APKs for authorized security analysis with apktool.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: AI review found the static alerts are caused by markdown command examples, inline code formatting, and legitimate APK signing guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, hidden network access, credential exfiltration, or executable malicious logic in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Command examples use user-provided APK paths and output directories.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to quote paths, validate that files are APKs, and ask before using overwrite flags or writing new output directories.

remediation.issue: APK signing examples reference local keystore files.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to use disposable debug keys for testing and never expose release keystore files or passwords in prompts.

remediation.issue: APK reverse engineering is dual-use security work.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the authorization requirement prominent before decoding, modifying, testing, or redistributing APK files.

content.value_statement: APK reviews need readable manifests, resources, and smali output. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through apktool analysis and rebuild workflows.
actual_capabilities: Decodes APK files with apktool into organized output directories.
Explains the decoded APK structure, including manifests, resources, assets, smali, and native libraries.
Guides searches for permissions, exported components, URLs, credentials, and security flags.
Supports resource-only and code-only decoding for faster analysis.
Documents rebuild, signing, verification, and zipalign steps for modified APKs.
Provides troubleshooting steps for framework, resource, memory, and signing errors.
limitations: Requires apktool and Java to be installed on the local system.
Does not decompile smali into readable Java source by itself.
Cannot determine whether the user has legal permission to analyze an APK.
Some obfuscated or damaged APKs may still produce incomplete output.

use_cases.title: Review Android App Security
use_cases.description: Decode an APK and inspect permissions, exported components, debuggable flags, backup settings, and network security configuration.

use_cases.title: Investigate IoT Companion Apps
use_cases.description: Extract endpoints, API references, device communication code, and certificate pinning clues from an authorized IoT app review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test APK Builds
use_cases.description: Rebuild modified resources or smali into a test APK, then sign and verify it before controlled installation.

prompt_templates.title: Decode an APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Use apktool to decode this APK into a new output directory. Explain the command, expected files, and first checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Manifest Security
prompt_templates.prompt: After decoding the APK, inspect AndroidManifest.xml for risky permissions, exported components, backup settings, debuggable flags, and SDK versions.

prompt_templates.title: Search Resources and Smali
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the decoded APK for URLs, API keys, tokens, passwords, crypto usage, and device communication classes. Summarize findings with file paths.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild and Sign Test APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Rebuild the modified APK with apktool, sign it with a disposable debug key, verify the signature, and explain any install issues.

output_examples.input: Decode app.apk and tell me where to start the review.
output_examples.output: The APK is decoded into an output folder. Start with the manifest, then review resources, smali packages, assets, and native libraries.

output_examples.input: Find security concerns in the decoded manifest.
output: Lists requested permissions and explains sensitive ones.
Highlights exported activities, services, and receivers.
Checks backup, debuggable, cleartext traffic, and SDK settings.

output_examples.input: My rebuilt APK will not install.
output_examples.output: The skill checks signing, verification, zipalign, resource build errors, and framework dependencies before suggesting the next repair step.

best_practices: Analyze only APKs you own or have permission to test.
Work on copies and keep decoded output in a dedicated directory.
Use disposable signing keys for test builds unless a release process is explicitly approved.
anti_patterns: Do not decode, modify, or redistribute third-party APKs without authorization.
Do not paste release keystore passwords or private signing keys into prompts.
Do not force overwrite output directories before checking their contents.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It guides apktool workflows for decoding, inspecting, rebuilding, and troubleshooting Android APK files.

faq.question: Does it require local tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The local system needs apktool and a Java Runtime Environment.

faq.question: Can it read Java source code?
faq.answer: Apktool produces smali, resources, and manifests. Use jadx with it when readable Java output is needed.

faq.question: Can it find hardcoded secrets?
faq.answer: It can guide searches for likely secrets, URLs, and tokens in decoded resources and smali files.

faq.question: Can it rebuild a modified APK?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains apktool rebuild steps and the signing steps required before installation.

faq.question: Is this only for security professionals?
faq.answer: It is intended for authorized security testing, research, debugging, and education with permission.
